I have the draft plan for deterministic skill-list ordering in context, along with your constraints: this invocation is for the review-mode decision only, the full mode name goes in the audit record and handoff line, and Office Hours, setup, and the substantive review are deferred. I'll wait for your slash command before taking any action.
I'll run the skill preamble first, then do the pre-review audit and Step 0 up through the mode-selection question, stopping there per your instruction.
Aside is not installed, so the landscape check falls back to one read-only WebSearch query.

The repo only has PLAN.md/CLAUDE.md with no prior context, and the actual listing code isn't in this checkout, so I confirmed via web research the standard fix: sort entries by code point/bytes (not locale) with a stable tie-break to avoid readdir-order fallback. I'll proceed in HOLD SCOPE mode, applying max rigor to just the comparator, case handling, tie-breaking, and the enumeration-order test across the ~2-3 affected files.

The mode decision is recorded. HOLD SCOPE was auto-selected from your saved preference for the mode question, so no menu was shown.

**Provenance.** The preference check for the mode question returned AUTO_DECIDE. The recommendation was HOLD SCOPE because the draft is a fix with a hard "outputs unchanged" invariant and an estimated 2 to 3 changed files. The audit record was written with the full mode name in both the user_choice and recommended fields, flagged as auto-decided, under this session's ID.

**Deferred per your instructions:**
- The Office Hours offer was not made, since no design doc exists and you said you would handle it separately.
- The skill-start output carried a one-time setup prompt to add skill routing rules to CLAUDE.md. That is setup, and plan mode also forbids editing CLAUDE.md or committing, so it stays pending and will re-fire on the next healthy run.
- The substantive review (0G HOLD SCOPE checks, 0I, Sections 1 to 11, report) has not started. No plan file was written and ExitPlanMode was not called, since the workflow is paused rather than complete.

**For the later review, two facts to carry forward:** the listing code is not in this checkout, so the real codebase is needed for the existing-code and file-count checks. The web research points to code-point sorting with a stable tie-break and warns against locale collation, which is the main design question HOLD SCOPE should pin down.

Telemetry is off for this install. No durable learnings this session.
